transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonas Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Sundial Biz Dev), Ravi Menon (Sundial CTO), Priya Kapoor (Sundial Cloud Architect)
Shared artifacts: Sundial marketplace reqs (Lena/sent after), Redwood partner one-pager https://redwood.ai/partners/p1 (referenced), quick bench commands (Jonas to share)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, AE on partner growth, and Jonas is our SE who will do the deep technical follow ups.
[00:12] Lena: Hi Maya, yeah thanks. I'm Lena, I run channel ops at Sundial. we do edge compute + managed SaaS for telco and retail, and exploring resell/marketplace opportunities.
[00:20] Ravi: Ravi here, CTO. interested in how Redwood would work with our hybrid deployments, and what the support model looks like.
[00:30] Priya: Priya, cloud architect. I want clarity on VPC, cross-account networking, and KMS key flows.
[00:40] Maya: great — agenda: quick intros, Redwood product modes (hosted / dedicated / private), how partner marketplace/reseller listing typically works, pilot scope, and open Qs on security/compliance. sound ok?
[00:55] Everyone: yup

[01:05] Jonas: I'll kick off lightly on the runtime side. Redwood has three serving modes: hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated pools for reserved capacity, and Private — which is basically a customer-controlled control plane in their VPC or on-prem package. For partners we usually recommend Private for regulated customers because you get network isolation and control of keys.
[01:30] Ravi: When you say Private, is that single-tenant in our VPC or do you run a managed control plane? we need to know where customer data travels.
[01:40] Jonas: good q — by default the control plane can be Redwood-managed but we offer an option where the control plane sits in your account (priv control plane) so the sensitive metadata and audit logs stay in your region. payloads can be restricted to stay inside your network. there's also an on-prem bundle if air-gap is required.
[02:05] Priya: And KMS — can we bring our key? our compliance requires CMKs in our HSM.
[02:12] Jonas: yes we have KMS integrations and customer-managed keys are supported; in the priv control plane we can wire to your KMS so Redwood doesn't hold the root key. there are a few config options — I'll send the integration notes.

[02:30] Lena: For marketplace listing: two things — our dev marketplace wants a lightweight integration (API + billing hook) and a co-marketing pack. what's typical for Redwood partners?
[02:45] Maya: we have a partner onboarding flow: partner profile, sales materials, API key provisioning with scoped roles, and a partner billing hook for marketplace invoicing. margins are negotiable — usually we align on list price and partner discount. we can provide a standard reseller addendum template.
[03:10] Lena: cool. our legal folks will want to see SOC2/ISO and data residency guarantees.
[03:17] Maya: we'll send SOC2, pen test summaries, and our standard compliance packet after this call.

[03:30] Jonas: one thing to flag — when partners resell dedicated/private, we usually carve out two integration patterns: 1) Sundial resells Redwood-hosted credits and controls billing end-to-end (low integration effort), or 2) Sundial bundles Redwood Private into their offering and co-manages deployment in customer accounts (more technical work but higher margin).
[03:55] Ravi: Hm margin question — can you share ballpark economics? like delta between hosted credits resale vs co-managed private?
[04:05] Maya: yes — I'll share a sample pricing model. generally reseller of hosted credits is lower margin but faster to market. Private co-managed has larger margin but requires onboarding and ops support.

[04:30] Priya: Onboarding timeline: if we want to run a pilot, what's realistic? we need to test latency for our edge use case and verify KV-cache behavior with burst traffic.
[04:42] Jonas: typical pilot is 4–6 weeks. first week: sandbox provisioning and baseline bench, weeks 2–4: workload run and optimization (batching, cache, quant), last 1–2 weeks: cutover checks and SLO validation. I can provide benchmark commands and a cost/latency template.
[04:58] Lena: ok 6 weeks sounds fine. we'll need an NDA/partner agreement in place before we share customer-level test data.
[05:08] Maya: understood. we'll send the NDA + reseller addendum.

[05:20] [short audio glitch]
[05:27] Ravi: what's the fallback story if the private cluster loses capacity — do you have autoscaling or fallback to a hosted model?
[05:36] Jonas: we support autoscaling within Dedicated/Private pools. for critical apps customers can define fallback policies that route to a lower-cost hosted variant in another region. this is configurable in the rollout policy. note that when crossing environments you might see latency variance.
[06:00] Priya: That was my concern — our customers value predictable tail latency. can you share percentile numbers?
[06:08] Jonas: we'll share our per-model perf profiles; for example a gen-XX 7B on A100 equiv typically hits 95th percentile sub-200ms in dedicated tuned envs at small seq lengths, but it depends on batch sizes and KV cache hit rates. I'll send profiling data — it's approximate, and we can run the exact bench on your workload.

[06:35] Lena: any legal quirks if we list Redwood on Sundial marketplace? how are trademarks and logos handled?
[06:44] Maya: we have a brand kit and marketplace listing guide, we'll share a PDF. standard co-marketing playbook is available.

[06:55] Ravi: ok technical nit — for the sandbox pilot, what endpoints should we hit and what telemetry will you expose? we need token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency.
[07:07] Jonas: sandbox will expose the same API surface as production. telemetry: token-level cost, per-route latency, per-model token counts, and trace hooks. we'll also hand over a Prometheus-compatible exporter if you want to ingest metrics into your stack.

[07:30] Priya: do you support mutual TLS between our service and the private control plane?
[07:34] Jonas: yes mTLS is supported for control plane and we can do private peering, VPC endpoints, and cross-account roles for infra ops. I'll add the network patterns doc to the follow-up.

[07:50] [brief cross talk]

[08:05] Lena: So next: I'll gather marketplace requirements and send them. we want the pilot to exercise our edge nodes — can Redwood run a bench that simulates geo-distributed bursts?
[08:20] Jonas: we can script distributed clients from multiple regions in the bench; we can also test caching effectiveness with prefix reuse.
[08:30] Ravi: What about upgrade and patch windows? we can't have forced restarts during retail peak hours.
[08:36] Jonas: we do scheduled maintenance windows and can pin model versions to avoid surprise rollouts. for Dedicated/Private customers we offer blackout windows and coordinated upgrades.

[08:50] Maya: quick commercial framing — partner pilot pricing can be metered with credits; if Sundial wants to move to a committed RS for Dedicated/Private we can discuss a partner discount and revenue share.
[09:06] Lena: good. our biz lead will want a template to review.

[09:15] [longer pause while files are referenced]

[09:40] Maya: to recap — Redwood will: 1) send partner onboarding pack, SOC2 and security packet, brand kit; 2) Jonas will send bench commands, perf profiles, and network/KMS integration notes; 3) Sundial will share marketplace reqs and legal contact for reseller addendum.
[10:05] Lena: yep, and we'll respond with a preferred pilot start window in Jan.

[10:12] Maya: any other questions?
[10:15] Ravi: one more — do you have references of other channel partners who've bundled Private? just for us to talk to.
[10:22] Maya: yes we can share a short list, will include contacts if ok.
[10:28] Priya: thanks all — environmental question: we have customers with strict data residency in EU — do you have region-local deploys?
[10:35] Jonas: yes we have region-local private deployments and can host in eu-west and other partner regions.

[10:45] Maya: awesome — thanks everyone for the time. we'll follow up with the packet and set the se deep dive.
[10:53] All: thanks, bye.
